Calls for Infantino's resignation have reached a fever pitch. Trump has intervened publicly on Truth Social to defend Infantino. North Korean ballistic missiles were used in strikes on Zaporizhzhia, killing seven civilian workers at the Metinvest steel plant and injuring 21; three more civilians including a 15-year-old boy were killed by Russian drones and artillery. Zelenskyy also warns Putin will use the Russian election — in which opposition to the war is banned — as a pretext for a major troop call-up. Separately, Putin has ordered a probe following the humiliation of Russia's Navy Day parade. Russia has released former US Marine Robert Gilman, 32, after more than four years in prison; Putin granted a humanitarian pardon and Trump is credited with securing the release. The State Department stated explicitly that no prisoner exchange took place and Washington made no concessions. Fox News had framed the release as a prisoner exchange, which the US government has now denied. Gilman had been in a dissociative stupor for 47 days and was gravely ill; his father disputes the Russian account of his arrest. Trump has signed an executive order overhauling the childhood vaccine schedule, drawing pushback from doctors, pharma, and public health experts. A 7.4-magnitude earthquake — Colombia's strongest on record — has struck western Colombia, killing at least 224–240 people and leaving more than 3,000 missing; rescuers are racing to find survivors amid fears the death toll will rise steeply. The Trump administration has pledged $15.5 million in relief.
